source.title: TIPS: Topologically Important Path Sampling for Anytime Neural Networks
source.authors: Gui-Hong Li; K. Bhardwaj; Yue-Dong Yang; R. Marculescu

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports training-loss convergence for an altered subnetwork-sampling training method, but it does not measure the training classification error or the other specific outcomes named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss convergence comparisons and test-accuracy results. Its pruning and accuracy-FLOPs results concern test performance, not the training-error claim. Its discussion of other initialization and topology studies is cited prior work, not this study's result.
record.test_reason: The study uses gradient-propagation and initialization principles related to V4 to motivate TIPS, then evaluates its own sampling method. Its training-loss comparisons, test accuracies, and topology–Jacobian correlations do not test any stated version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that TIPS accelerates training convergence relative to compared anytime-inference methods and improves test-accuracy–FLOPs tradeoffs.
record.recipe_differences: TIPS changes subnetwork operation-sampling probabilities during training; the compared claim concerns gradient-based training outcomes such as training classification error, initialization, depth, and normalization.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that too high a sampling probability for important operations can hurt subnetwork diversity and test accuracy; it uses a 50% higher sampling probability for important operations.

fits_no_version.finding: MobileNet-v2 TIPS reaches training loss below 1.25 on ImageNet in 88 epochs versus 145 for US-Nets; Tiny-ImageNet convergence is also reported as faster than US-Nets and Joslim.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Topology-informed subnetwork sampling can reduce epochs to a training-loss target in the tested anytime supernets.

fits_no_version.finding: For residual MLP supernets with 80–140 layers, sampled 50-node paths with higher TPS have higher mean Jacobian singular values, closer to one within each supernet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: TPS predicts mean Jacobian singular values of fixed-length paths within the tested residual MLP supernets.

record.problems: The convergence evidence is shown in a figure; the text gives numeric target-loss epochs only for ImageNet. Results concern training loss rather than training classification error, and the paper does not state initialization details for these runs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows needed for the claim versions. Test-accuracy and accuracy-FLOPs tables, operation-pruning accuracy plots, and topology metric experiments do not measure the training-error outcomes specified by the versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random or corrupted labels, and dependence on model size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training-error degradation in plain networks and its prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.

Effects of activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and initialization-dependent learning speed or trainable depth. The topology–Jacobian analysis does not compare initialization schemes.
Recovery above an initial stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence conditions.
Training-speed and learning-rate-tolerance comparisons with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its correctly unlinked rows. Initialization and dynamical-isometry principles are used in the analysis, but their effects on learning speed or trainable depth are not independently tested.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and the listed CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training-error conditions are not measured. CIFAR100 results are test accuracy.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or spurious-minima outcome.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison of training error.
No comparison of initialization schemes or trainable depth by initialization.
No learning-rate stability-threshold or sharpness experiment.

rows.subject: MobileNet-v2-based supernet
rows.operation_detail: Uniform subnetwork operation-sampling training; reports epochs to reach training loss below 1.25.
rows.note: This is a training-loss convergence measure, not training classification error.
rows.check: The 145-epoch value is correctly reported, but it measures a baseline sampling method's time to a composite training-loss target, not near-zero training classification error. Appendix B.2 combines cross-entropy and distillation losses.

rows.subject: MobileNet-v2-based supernet
rows.operation_detail: TIPS subnetwork operation-sampling training; reports epochs to reach training loss below 1.25.
rows.note: This is a training-loss convergence measure, not training classification error.
rows.check: The 88-epoch value and 145-epoch comparator are correct. This is the study's own sampling method compared with a baseline, with no initialization, normalization, or stability-threshold intervention; it should remain outside claim evidence.

rows.subject: MobileNet-v2-based supernet
rows.operation_detail: Uniform subnetwork operation-sampling training; training-loss curve compared with TIPS.
rows.note: The text says TIPS needs much fewer epochs to achieve a target training loss; it gives no numerical value for these baselines on Tiny-ImageNet.
rows.check: This combines US-Nets and Joslim into one row; separate them if retaining method-performance rows. Figure 5(c) and the accompanying text establish a qualitative convergence comparison, but provide no precise target-loss epochs in the supplied text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
